subject: Immediate kernel rollout impacting inference runtime — action requested
messages:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Alex Johnson <alex@scaleapps.com>, support@scaleapps.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Immediate kernel rollout impacting inference runtime — action requested

Hi Alex / ScaleApps team,

We’re pushing an emergency kernel rollout to a subset of GPU inference nodes in us-west-2 due to a discovered kernel-driver interaction that can cause elevated memory pressure on long-lived KV-cache sessions. We identified an increased risk of degraded tail latency for a small percentage of requests if left unpatched.

What’s happening now:
- Rollout start: 2029-04-11 09:10 PDT (already started as of this email).
- Scope: canary pool -> gradual rollout to remaining us-west-2 serving racks (expected < 45 minutes).
- Impact window: brief connection drain and service-level retries while nodes are rotated; some requests may experience increased p99 latency or transient 503s if they hit an affected host.

What we request from ScaleApps (action requested):
1) If you can, briefly divert heavy inference traffic away from the us-west-2 region for ~20–40 minutes to reduce exposure to retries during the canary.
2) Confirm if you have pinned model variants or pinned host-affinity settings — if so we’ll coordinate a manual drain for those hosts (we can pause rollout for your pinned hosts if needed).

If you can’t divert traffic, we will proceed with a conservative rollout and keep retries + graceful retry windows enabled. We’ve attached a short patch notes summary and rollback instructions; the patch includes a micro-kernel flag that remedies the memory pressure behavior.

Estimated next updates:
- Canary verification (first success/failure metrics): +15 minutes
- Full rollback or continue decision: +30–45 minutes

Apologies for the short notice — we moved quickly because the telemetry indicated rising memory footprint on a small number of nodes and we want to avoid a larger outage. I’ll be monitoring the rollout and will post continuous updates in this thread.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kernel_patch_notes_v1.pdf (summary of kernel flag and verification steps)
Attachment: rollback_instructions.txt (host-level rollback commands and safe drain steps)

From: Alex Johnson <alex@scaleapps.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: support@scaleapps.com
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:19:13 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate kernel rollout impacting inference runtime — action requested

Thanks for the heads-up, Jasmine.

We can divert bulk batch scoring jobs off us-west-2 within ~10 minutes; however real-time traffic will still hit us-west-2 (low latency requirement). A couple quick questions:
- ETA on when the canary metrics will be available? We’ll hold off the heavy jobs until you confirm success.
- How does the patch interact with our pinning? We do have a small set of pinned hosts for the 4x-quant models.

If you need an explicit opt-out for our pinned hosts, we can provide the host IDs — otherwise feel free to pause rollout for them. Appreciate the attachment.

—Alex
Alex Johnson, Platform Engineering
ScaleApps
alex@scaleapps.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, Alex Johnson <alex@scaleapps.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 09:28:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate kernel rollout impacting inference runtime — action requested

Alex —
We’ll pause the rollout for any pinned hosts once you provide the host IDs; please send them in a quick reply and we’ll exclude them from the canary.

Canary plan (short):
- 3 hosts in controlled canary with full traffic mirroring to internal verification cluster.
- Monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, kernel memory RSS.
- Hold/rollback criteria: sustained p99 > baseline + 200ms for > 5 minutes OR 5xx rate > 0.5% for the canary.

If all clear after 15 minutes we’ll expand at a conservative rate. Ben — please prepare the rollback sequence and be ready to execute if the canary crosses thresholds.

We’ll post the first verification in ~15 minutes.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

> On Thu, Apr 11, 2029 at 09:19 AM Alex Johnson <alex@scaleapps.com> wrote:
> > Thanks for the heads-up...

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Alex Johnson <alex@scaleapps.com>, support@scaleapps.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2029 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate kernel rollout impacting inference runtime — action requested

Update (final for this incident):

Status: Patch rolled out to all us-west-2 inference nodes at 12:07 PDT. Canary passed verification at 09:34 PDT (p99 and 5xx within thresholds). We expanded at a conservative cadence and did not hit rollback criteria.

Impact observed: A small subset of requests hitting affected hosts experienced elevated p99 (~230ms above baseline) during the canary window and there were isolated transient 503s while nodes drained. The overall customer-facing error rate stayed under 0.25% for the region.

Customer actions taken: Thank you for diverting batch jobs — we excluded the pinned hosts for ScaleApps per your host-ID list and the rollout proceeded on the rest of the fleet. No additional action required from ScaleApps at this time.

Follow-up: We will publish a short postmortem with telemetry graphs, root cause, and remediation steps by EOD tomorrow. Interim artifacts and the exact verification output are available here: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/ops/incident-kernel-rollout-20290411.md

If you notice any residual errors or anomalous behavior in the next 24 hours please escalate directly to our on-call: +1 (555) 212-0420 or ops@redwood.ai and reference this thread id.

Apologies again for the short notice and thank you for the rapid coordination.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
